world.h: Ukrainian drones hit St Petersburg, killing 1
world.b: Firefighters battled blazes at the St Petersburg oil terminal, the Ruchi oil depot and industrial warehouses, and several residential buildings were hit. The attack disrupted flights at the city's main airport.
world.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s St Petersburg kills 1, hits energy sites

world.h: Rubio: Ukraine lacks Starshield access for now
world.b: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Kyiv's request to use the Starshield military satellite system for attacks deep inside Russia is 'under discussion,' stressing it is a defence product, unlike the commercial Starlink.
world.title: Rubio says Ukraine without access to Starshield, future ‘under discussion’

world.h: Iran says two tankers hit mines in Hormuz
world.b: Two tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's IRGC and the IRNA news agency said. IRNA said the vessels had switched off their positioning and radar systems; their names were not released.

world.h: US and Iran both claim control of Hormuz
world.b: Washington and Tehran each say they control the Strait of Hormuz amid attacks on vessels. UK maritime monitor UKMTO says it is struggling to count attacks because most targeted ships refuse to report them.

world.h: Iran war: Egypt pledges support to Saudi Arabia
world.b: Al Jazeera's live coverage: Egypt says it will give Saudi Arabia 'necessary support' following Houthi attacks on the kingdom.
world.title: Egypt ready to give Saudi Arabia ‘necessary support’ after Houthi attacks

national.b: Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old carpenter, fired his legally stored pistol after seeing a teacher fighting the shooter at his daughters' school in Bend, police said. Such armed interventions remain rare.

national.h: No Kings shifts focus to early voting
national.b: Grassroots groups plan more than 3,000 "No Kings: Vote Early" marches and events Saturday to help people register and plan their ballots.

politics.h: Vance pressed on Iran war at CBS town hall
politics.b: Vice President JD Vance faced pointed questions on the Iran war and immigration, including one from the widow of a soldier killed by an Iranian drone in Kuwait. He said there is 'of course' a chance he doesn't run in 2028.
politics.title: Vance faces tough questions on Iran war, immigration and more in CBS town hall

politics.h: Trump to close D.C. golf course for renovation
politics.b: Trump said the historic course near the White House will close starting Nov. 15 for 15 months of work, though a judge has halted the redevelopment until at least Oct. 26 over tree removal.
politics.title: Trump says he will close historic D.C. golf course for 15 months of renovations

politics.h: GOP governor hopefuls soften abortion stances
politics.b: Pennsylvania's Stacy Garrity says she would 'respect' the state's current abortion law, and Kansas's Ty Masterson has demurred on a referendum to remove the state constitution's abortion protections.
politics.title: The Republican governor candidates walking back some of their abortion stances

politics.h: US Jews divided as Israel's election nears
politics.b: Many Orthodox Jews back Netanyahu as protecting Israel, while many liberal and younger Jewish Americans say his policies have harmed Israel's global standing, as antisemitism rises in the U.S.

politics.h: Congress outraged as Trump waives Russia sanctions
politics.b: Lawmakers in both parties criticized Trump's order pausing sanctions on the Russian economy, with Sen. Thom Tillis calling it 'beyond irresponsible,' but no quick counter is expected. Zelenskyy urged support for the sanctions.

politics.h: Speaker Johnson draws on faith to hold House
politics.b: House Speaker Mike Johnson is leaning on his recruits, his fundraising for House Republicans and his faith as he fights to keep the GOP majority. 'We run to win, and that's biblical,' he said in Maine.

politics.h: Trump vowed swing-district blitz, visits red states
politics.b: Trump pledged to campaign in 35 competitive races but has campaigned with fewer than a third of those candidates.

politics.h: DOJ warns California officials on ballots
politics.b: A Justice Department letter says officials who process mail ballots from suspected noncitizens risk prosecution, a day after the administration sued the state.

international.h: Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of Israeli vote
international.b: Nine days before Israel's election, Trump gave his 'Complete and Total Endorsement' to Benjamin Netanyahu, praising him as an ally in the war on Iran.
international.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israeli legislative elections

international.h: Pope Leo to gradually resume duties
international.b: Appearing at his window over St. Peter's Square for the Angelus, Pope Leo said he will gradually resume his activities after lung surgery, saying the experience made him feel close to those facing illness.
international.title: Pope Leo tells faithful in St. Peter's Square he will gradually resume duties after cancer surgery

international.h: Gaza prices surge as Israel halts commercial goods
international.b: Flour, eggs, onions and other staples have sharply risen in price since Wednesday, when Israel said commercial goods would no longer enter Gaza amid a dispute over fees. Families are stocking up for fear of shortages.
international.title: Gaza families fear food shortages as Israel halts commercial shipments

international.h: Funeral held for 75 Palestinians found in Gaza ruins
international.b: Hundreds attended as remains recovered from destroyed buildings were buried at Sheikh Radwan Cemetery. Most of the victims were from the Daraj neighbourhood, the Ministry of Health said.
international.title: Funeral held for 75 Palestinians after remains recovered from Gaza ruins

international.h: 4 killed in fire at Alberta military base
international.b: Prime Minister Mark Carney said four service members were killed and dozens injured at CFB Wainwright, where fierce winds pushed flames into the surrounding area. The military said there was no indication of terrorism.
international.title: Carney says 4 service members killed and dozens injured in fire at Alberta military base

international.h: Former Guatemalan prosecutor shot dead
international.b: Former prosecutor Foppa and another man were killed in an attack at the Campo Marte sports complex in Guatemala City. Police said they arrested two men and seized a firearm and a motorcycle.

international.h: Kenya confirms four more Ebola cases
international.b: Kenya's Ebola total has risen to seven. Three of the new cases are health workers who treated the country's first patient, and the fourth is a relative of that patient, who died, the Ministry of Health said.

international.h: How Alberta separatism reached a referendum
international.b: Alberta is voting on a path toward separation from Canada. Premier Danielle Smith, who called the vote but backs staying in Canada, says support for starting the process is 'still too high for my liking.'

international.h: Masked settlers attack European diplomats
international.b: Settlers in the West Bank village of Taybeh targeted Belgium's consul general, French and Polish diplomats and Catholic representatives, Belgium's foreign minister said. A French mayor was assaulted and a Belgian vehicle damaged.

international.h: Biggest protest in years against Tunisia's Saied
international.b: Thousands marched against President Kais Saied, backed by the UGTT trade union federation, opposition parties and civil society groups. AFP put the crowd at more than 3,000.

international.h: Pope Leo returns to Vatican after surgery
international.b: Pope Leo, 71, left hospital four days after having the lower lobe of his right lung removed. His surgeon said there is no clinical reason he cannot make his Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Peru and Argentina.

international.h: Protesters clash with police across France
international.b: Riot police used tear gas against hooded, masked protesters in Paris as nationwide demonstrations spread, with dozens reportedly detained around Place de la Republique. In Marseille, local media said protesters breached the town hall.

international.h: Settlers injure child, four women in West Bank
international.b: Israeli settlers attacked residents of Ma'in village in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron, injuring six people including four women and a child, the Palestine Red Crescent said. Elsewhere, Israeli forces fired on olive-picking farmers near Ramallah, Wafa reported.

international.h: Israeli rabbi's olive ruling sparks uproar
international.b: Prominent rabbi Dov Lior issued a religious ruling permitting settlers to take olives from Palestinian orchards in the occupied West Bank, arguing landowners blocked from their harvests had been 'compensated' in earlier years.

international.h: Egypt's Sisi offers defence help to Saudi Arabia
international.b: Speaking at an Egyptian Military Academy graduation, President el-Sisi said Egypt is ready to 'carry out any measure to protect' Saudi Arabia if Riyadh asks, and is seeking authorisation for defence assistance.

international.h: Solar booms in Philippines as Iran war lifts power bills
international.b: Electricity prices have soared since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February, pushing a growing number of Filipino households to install rooftop solar panels to cut their bills.

international.h: South Africans seek justice for apartheid crimes
international.b: Decades after apartheid ended, families of victims, including those killed when police opened fire on protesters on March 21, 1960, are still pressing for accountability in a neglected township near Johannesburg.
international.title: Decades after apartheid, South Africans seek justice for crimes of the past

international.h: Russian attacks kill 8, cut power to 1 million
international.b: Strikes on nine Ukrainian regions hit two shopping centres. In Kharkiv, two people were killed and 12 wounded, the governor said.

international.h: Sudan army claims strikes on RSF in Nyala
international.b: The army says dozens of RSF fighters were killed in South Darfur. The RSF says a drone hit a livestock market, killing 30 civilians.

international.h: IMF urges help for poorer nations hit by war
international.b: Kristalina Georgieva said as annual meetings ended in Bangkok that low-income countries face rising debt, high inflation and war spillovers.

international.h: Israel's opposition unites against Netanyahu
international.b: Yair Lapid, Naftali Bennett, Gadi Eisenkot, Yair Golan and Avigdor Liberman met in Tel Aviv and published shared principles ahead of the Oct. 27 election.

international.h: Three jailed 158 years for killing surfers
international.b: A judge in Ensenada sentenced three men for the 2024 murders of Australian brothers Callum and Jake Robinson and their American friend Jack Carter Rhoad.

international.h: US Coast Guard rescues 16 after boat sinks off Baja
international.b: The boat went down about 140 miles west of Ensenada. A search continues for 11 people believed missing.

international.h: Cameroonians await reshuffle after Biya's return
international.b: President Paul Biya, 93, returned in August after about 10 weeks abroad, but no new government has been named and the vice presidency remains vacant.

business.h: Couples turn to grocery store wedding cakes
business.b: With weddings averaging about $36,000 according to Zola, some couples are skipping specialty bakers, which can charge more than $1,000, for half sheet cakes from Costco at about $30 each.
business.title: Weddings are expensive. How about a grocery store cake?

science.h: Nature funding falls short before UN summit
science.b: Countries are behind on raising $200 billion a year for biodiversity as the COP17 talks open Monday to review the 2022 "30x30" targets.

sports.h: Ole Miss earns an 'A' in commanding win
sports.b: Kewan Lacy ran for 122 yards and Trinidad Chambliss accounted for four touchdowns as Ole Miss improved to 5-1. Georgia got an 'F' after its loss to Auburn.
sports.title: College football grades: Ole Miss earns 'A' for commanding win, Georgia gets 'F' on Week 7 report card

sports.h: Big 12 admits clock error in BYU-Notre Dame finish
sports.b: The Big 12 said Notre Dame should have had one second left for another play after CJ Carr's final heave fell incomplete and BYU fans stormed the field.

sports.h: BYU makes case for No. 1 after beating Notre Dame
sports.b: In a chaotic Week 7, No. 8 BYU beat No. 2 Notre Dame while No. 1 Georgia lost to unranked Auburn and Texas fell to unranked Florida, setting up a shake-up atop the rankings.

sports.h: Auburn stuns No. 1 Georgia on walk-off field goal
sports.b: Alex McPherson's field goal as time expired gave Auburn a 27-24 win after Georgia led 14-0, snapping the Bulldogs' 54-game winning streak against unranked teams.
Ohio State ended Indiana's 22-game win streak when a late fourth-down catch by Nick Marsh landed out of bounds, but quarterback Julian Sayin's injury may shape the Buckeyes' season.

sports.h: Florida stuns No. 7 Texas in Austin
sports.b: The Gators rallied behind running back Jadan Baugh to hand the Longhorns a second straight loss, one week after Texas fell in the Red River game.

sports.h: Southern Nazarene's Tyler Ulrich dies at 21
sports.b: The sophomore defensive player died after five days in hospital following an injury in last week's game at Ouachita Baptist. Saturday's game against Southwestern Oklahoma State was canceled.
Wil Lutz's field goal won it after a Sam Darnold interception. Analyst Ryan Fitzpatrick ripped Bo Nix, who threw for 107 yards.

sports.h: Brewers sweep Dodgers, reach World Series
sports.b: Milwaukee won Game 4 6-4 to complete the NLCS sweep. Jake Bauers, with six RBI in the series, was named NLCS MVP.
FIFA president Gianni Infantino apologized over this year's World Cup controversies, but European delegates said "no satisfactory answers were provided."

sports.h: Caleb Williams pushes back on injury reports
sports.b: The Bears quarterback is on track for a possible Week 6 return from his hamstring injury but said he still doesn't know if he'll play Sunday against Atlanta.

sports.h: Eagles place Jalen Hurts on injured reserve
sports.b: Hurts, dealing with a superficial blood clot, will miss at least four weeks, including games against the Panthers, Cowboys, Commanders and Giants. Tanner McKee will lead the offense.

local.b: A four-alarm fire scorched a commercial building on Hylan Boulevard, injuring two people including a firefighter, but the nearby Old Church of St. Joachim and St. Anne was not damaged, the FDNY said.
local.title: Staten Island fire injures two, but spares historic 'Godfather' church

local.h: Bail reform still central in NY governor's race
local.b: Seven years after it became law, bail reform remains a major issue in the governor's race, with opponents pointing to cases like a Rochester man who fired at an officer while out on bail.
local.title: Bail reform remains major issue in NY governor's race, 7 years after it became law

local.h: Man shot near Midtown subway station
local.b: A man was shot Saturday afternoon near the 53rd Street and 7th Avenue station, which serves the B, D and E lines, the NYPD said. Police released no other details, and his condition was unclear.
local.title: NYPD searching for 'person of interest' in fatal Midtown subway platform shooting

local.h: NYPD seeks Yorkie dognapped in Queens
local.b: Chanel, a 10-year-old Yorkshire Terrier, was taken from her front lawn in College Point late last month when two people in a Subaru Forester scooped her up and sped off, police said.
local.title: Have you seen this Yorkie? NYPD looking for adorable pup dognapped from her Queens home

local.h: Knicks fans adjust to life as champions
local.b: After winning the 2026 NBA Championship, the Knicks will raise their first championship banner at Madison Square Garden in 50 years as they open their season.
local.title: Being reigning champions is weird for Knicks fans, but we could get used to this.

local.h: Tompkins Square Park makeover splits regulars
local.b: A community board committee backed renovating the basketball courts, kids' pool and 1990s outdoor fitness area. Some park users say it goes too far.
local.title: Tompkins Square Park is getting a makeover. Some say it's too much.

periods.text: Increasing clouds, with a high near 63. Northeast wind around 10 mph.

periods.text: Mostly cloudy, with a low around 54. North wind 10 to 17 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday
periods.text: Mostly sunny, with a high near 65. North wind 15 to 17 mph.

periods.name: Tuesday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 51. Breezy.
